claims.claim_text: The PyTorch Foundation announced the release of PyTorch 2.15.
claims.excerpt: We are excited to announce the release of PyTorch® 2.15 (release notes)!

claims.claim_text: In PyTorch 2.15, the rewritten NCCL backend is the default for every nccl process group, with TORCH_DIST_USE_NCCL2=0 and the nccl-legacy backend name as rollback paths.
claims.excerpt: In 2.15 it is the default for every nccl process group, with TORCH_DIST_USE_NCCL2=0 and the nccl-legacy backend name as rollback paths.

claims.claim_text: The PyTorch 2.15 release is composed of 3,117 commits from 583 contributors since PyTorch 2.14.
claims.excerpt: This release is composed of 3,117 commits from 583 contributors since PyTorch 2.14.

claims.claim_text: The default PyTorch wheel moves to CUDA 13.2, with CUDA 13.4 GA wheels shipping alongside it.
claims.excerpt: The default PyTorch wheel moves to CUDA 13.2 (13.2.2 toolkit), with CUDA 13.4 GA wheels shipping alongside it for Linux x86_64, Linux aarch64 and Windows.

claims.claim_text: PyTorch 2.15 requires Python 3.11 or newer, and Python 3.10 is no longer supported.
claims.excerpt: Python 3.10 is no longer supported. PyTorch 2.15 requires Python 3.11 or newer

claims.claim_text: PyTorch 2.15 requires macOS 15 or newer for MPS acceleration, dropping macOS 14 support.
claims.excerpt: PyTorch 2.15 requires macOS 15 or newer for MPS (Apple Silicon GPU) acceleration.

claims.claim_text: PyTorch says that on an M3 Ultra, the new MPS grouped_mm gemv path gives 1.32–1.34x higher MoE decode throughput.
claims.excerpt: the new MPS grouped_mm has a gemv path that gives 1.32–1.34x higher MoE decode throughput on an M3 Ultra.

claims.claim_text: PyTorch says that NVGEMM with NVFP4 decode fuses the scalar dequantization factor into the GEMM, removing a separate pointwise launch per layer during decode.
claims.excerpt: now folds the scalar dequantization factor of ModelOpt NVFP4 linear layers into the GEMM, removing a separate pointwise launch per layer during decode.

claims.claim_text: PyTorch says the new flight recorder writes a post-mortem to disk when a collective hangs.
claims.excerpt: a backend-agnostic flight recorder writes a post-mortem to disk when a collective hangs

claims.claim_text: The new torch.distributed one-sided transport API has NIXL as its first backend.
claims.excerpt: torch.distributed gains a Python transport API for one-sided data movement, with NIXL as the first backend.
